rfi.title: Mediterranean migrant rescue ships threatened by Libyan groups, warns NGO
rfi.description: A leading group monitoring and providing aid to migrants crossing the Mediterranean have warned that its rescue ships have been facing increasing threats and harassment from Libyan groups.

rfi.title: Malian PM's visit to Algeria underlines need for mutual security goals
rfi.description: The acting head of the Malian government, General Abdoulaye Maiga has begun a two-day visit to Algeria. It comes amid a thaw after months of tension. RFI spoke to Bakary Sambe, the Director of the Timbuktu Institute about the security situation and what the countries hope to gain from the meeting.

rfi.title: Six million Somalis face acute hunger as drought and conflict worsen
rfi.description: Six million people in Somalia are facing acute hunger, with nearly two million children at emergency levels, as severe drought, conflict and falling humanitarian funding deepen what the UN describes as one of the world’s worst malnutrition crises. Medical charity MSF tells RFI it's sounding the alarm "before it's too late".

rfi.title: Violence against healthcare workers in DRC hampers Ebola response
rfi.description: Healthcare workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo have been coming under attack, the United Nations and Red Cross have warned, hampering efforts to stem the spread of the Ebola virus, which is spreading 'exponentially'.

rfi.title: France gathers Ukraine's allies to boost resistance to Russia
rfi.description: Countries allied with Ukraine in its war with Russia are meeting on Monday to reaffirm support for Kyiv and discuss how to pressure Moscow to halt its invasion, in talks held symbolically on Ukraine's independence day. French President Emmanuel Macron will co-chair the gathering of the so-called "Coalition of the Willing" via video link.

rfi.title: Centre-left Glucksmann enters French presidential race as left tries to unite
rfi.description: French centre-left politician Raphael Glucksmann has announced his candidacy for next year's presidential election, seeking to challenge hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon to lead France's fractured left, as a campaign increasingly dominated by the far right takes shape.

rfi.title: Scorching summer takes toll on bees and honey harvests in France
rfi.description: France produces 20,000 tonnes of honey each year, but successive heatwaves and persistent drought across Europe this summer are impacting bee populations as flowering plants dry out and colonies struggle to find food. Beekeeper Romain Lacotte and his family farm 1,000 hives in Haute-Corrèze, central France, an area considered one of the country's natural water towers. But even there, he tells RFI, high temperatures and lack of rain are taking their toll.

rfi.title: DRC and M23 rebels agree on roadmap for peace in eastern Congo
rfi.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo government and the M23 rebel group have agreed on a roadmap for peace talks aimed at resolving the protracted conflict in eastern DRC. It marks the latest step in an internationally brokered peace process that has seen the parties make cautious concessions, without ending the fighting.

rfi.title: Saudi crown prince heads to France as Paris seeks closer Gulf ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Sunday for a two-day official visit, as Paris looks to deepen ties with Riyadh against a backdrop of war in the Middle East.

rfi.title: Mystery elephant deaths in Kenya leave experts divided over cause
rfi.description: Conservationists and Maasai communities are calling for urgent answers as paralysis-like symptoms spread among elephants in Kenya's Amboseli National Park, with competing theories emerging over what is causing their deaths.

rfi.title: Togo says it has 'serious' evidence against detained French journalists
rfi.description: Togo's government says it has "serious and consistent evidence" against two French documentary filmmakers detained since July on charges of making false statements. Gaël Mocaër and Sebastian Perez Pezzani were arrested along with their Togolese fixer, Fred Vedomey, and have denied wrongdoing.

rfi.title: Southern African mothers plead for sons lured to Russia's war in Ukraine
rfi.description: Instead of celebrating her son's birthday this month, Zimbabwean mother Rodwin Chitewere spent the day praying for his body to be brought home from Russia, where he was reportedly killed fighting Moscow's war against Ukraine.

rfi.title: 'Niu Lai', the 'so bad it's good' Chinese cartoon becoming a box-office hit
rfi.description: An amateur animated film has become a surprise box-office hit in China, fuelling a wider debate about cinema, artificial intelligence and audience tastes. Made by a mother-and-son team on a shoestring budget, Niu Lai went from commercial failure to viral sensation after attracting a wave of negative reviews.

rfi.title: Eroding coastlines unearth and destroy slave graves in French Caribbean
rfi.description: Rising seas and coastal erosion are exposing the graves of enslaved people on beaches in the French Caribbean departments of Martinique and Guadeloupe, bringing long-buried remains back into view. Archaeologists say the retreating coastline is revealing new information about people who were enslaved centuries ago, but also destroying sites of historical and cultural importance.

rfi.title: France to send interceptor missiles to Ukraine after Russian strikes
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Saturday announced Paris would deliver new interceptor missiles to Ukraine, with Kyiv's air defences running short after the latest round of deadly Russian attacks.

rfi.title: Ravaged by wildfires, France's Fontainebleau forest reopens to public
rfi.description: The forest of Fontainebleau outside Paris has partially reopened to the public after remaining off-limits for over a month due to devastating wildfires. From Saturday, visitors can access some 80 percent of the forest, but are being warned to show caution around fragile wildlife and charred trees.

rfi.title: Diplomats urge France and UK to uphold rule of law in Palestinian territories
rfi.description: Dozens of former senior French and UK diplomats on Saturday urged their governments to work together to uphold international law in the Palestinian territories, accusing Israel of seeking to "destroy" any prospect of a viable Palestinian state.

rfi.title: Still waters run deep: why Palme d'or winner 'Fjord' questions our certainties
rfi.description: An isolated village in Norway sees its peaceful veneer upset by the arrival of a new family in Fjord, the Palme d'Or-winning film released in French cinemas this week. Inspired by real-life cases, Romanian director Cristian Mungiu explores questions of domestic violence, religion, culture and tolerance through a story that asks whose version of the truth can be trusted.

Il a été rejoint par l’influenceur niçois Nicolas Aragona connu, sous le pseudonyme « Supersero ».

lemonde.title: « Les autres habitants, vous les voyez jouer dans les rues à minuit ? » : à Moissac, une défiance mutuelle entre le maire RN et ses administrés bulgares
lemonde.description: « Venu(e)s d’ailleurs » (6/7). Plusieurs centaines de Bulgares vivent dans cette commune de Tarn-et Garonne, dirigée depuis 2020 par un édile Rassemblement national, qui cible dans ses discours une « immigration de peuplement ».

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Raphaël Glucksmann veut remporter la primaire socialiste sur une ligne anti-LFI
france24fr.description: Raphaël Glucksmann, désormais candidat à la primaire socialiste, a fait du rapport de la gauche à Jean-Luc Mélenchon et de la question d’une éventuelle alliance avec La France insoumise aux législatives de 2027 un élément central de son projet politique en vue des débats à venir face à ses concurrents.

france24fr.title: Ukraine : le pays fête ses 35 ans d’indépendance malgré la guerre
france24fr.description: L’Ukraine célèbre ce lundi les 35 ans de son indépendance. À Kiev, Volodymyr Zelensky a participé à une cérémonie devant la cathédrale Sainte-Sophie, marquée par une minute de silence en hommage aux soldats morts au combat. Plusieurs dirigeants européens ont également fait le déplacement.

france24fr.title: En RD Congo, une première mission de vérification du cessez-le-feu dans l'Est
france24fr.description: Alors que l'armée congolaise et le groupe politico-militaire AFC/M23, soutenu par le Rwanda, se sont mutuellement accusés d'exactions lundi, une première mission régionale de vérification d'un fragile cessez-le-feu entre les belligérants s'est déployée dans l'est de la République démocratique du Congo.

france24fr.title: Coalition des volontaires : comment mieux protéger l’Ukraine ?
france24fr.description: Les alliés de Kiev se réunissent à nouveau au sein de la Coalition des volontaires, alors que les attaques russes contre les civils s’intensifient. Vendredi, une frappe de drones contre un centre commercial a fait 19 morts et 130 blessés. Récit de Dorothée Olliéric (France 2).

france24fr.title: Ukraine : Kiev rassemble ses alliés autour des questions de défense
france24fr.description: Les alliés de Kiev se réunissent à nouveau au sein de la Coalition des volontaires pour renforcer la protection de l’Ukraine face à l’intensification des attaques russes. Décryptage de Bruno Daroux, chroniqueur international France 24.

france24fr.title: Iran : les partenaires de Téhéran dans le viseur de Washington
france24fr.description: Les États-Unis s’apprêtent à annoncer une nouvelle salve de sanctions contre l’Iran, mais aussi contre les pays, entreprises et institutions financières qui continueraient de commercer avec Téhéran. Donald Trump menace ces partenaires de "terribles conséquences économiques", dans le but d’accentuer l’isolement du régime iranien sans engager de nouvelle opération militaire. Correspondance de Sarah Andersen depuis New York pour France 24.

france24fr.title: Guinée : deux ministres proches du président limogés sur fond de lutte anticorruption
france24fr.description: 🇬🇳 En Guinée, deux ministres proches du président Mamadi Doumbouya ont été limogés vendredi. Mory Condé, chargé de l’Emploi, et Mourana Soumah, à la Communication quittent leurs fonctions sans détails sur les motifs de cette décision. Quelques heures plus tard, le chef de l’État a réaffirmé sur Facebook sa volonté de lutter contre la corruption.

france24fr.title: USS Donald Trump ou USS Doris Miller... la Navy va-t-elle effacer le nom d'un héros afro-américain ?
france24fr.description: L'un des prochains porte-avions américain doit porter le nom de Doris Miller, un marin qui s'est illustré lors de l'attaque de Pearl Harbor en décembre 1941. Mais selon plusieurs sources, la Marine envisagerait désormais de le baptiser plutôt du nom du président Donald Trump. Ces révélations suscitent un tollé outre-Atlantique.

france24fr.title: RD Congo : 100 jours après, l'épidémie d'Ebola reste difficile à contenir
france24fr.description: Cent jours après la déclaration officielle de la 17e épidémie d'Ebola en RD Congo, les autorités tentent de freiner la propagation du virus. En l'absence de vaccin contre la souche Boundi Bouguio, la prévention reste essentielle, notamment dans les lieux de travail où se côtoient des personnes venues de différentes régions.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : des ONG alertent sur la montée des discours xénophobes
france24fr.description: Les discours xénophobes se multiplient au Sénégal, notamment sur les réseaux sociaux. Face à la stigmatisation croissante des étrangers, des acteurs de la société civile tirent la sonnette d’alarme.

france24fr.title: "Le Canada ⁠ne sera plus traité comme un État !" : Trump durcit la guerre commerciale contre Ottawa
france24fr.description: Après l'échec des négociations commerciales avec Ottawa, Donald Trump a déclaré, lundi, ‌dans un message publié sur les ⁠réseaux sociaux que les droits ⁠de douane américains ​sur les voitures, les camions, les pièces détachées automobiles ​et l'acier produits au Canada seront portés à 50 % à compter du 1er janvier 2027.

france24fr.title: Macron reçoit MBS à Paris : l’énergie et la défense au cœur des échanges
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron reçoit à Paris le prince héritier saoudien Mohammed ben Salmane pour une journée de discussions diplomatiques et stratégiques. Les deux dirigeants doivent aborder les crises qui traversent le Moyen-Orient : la guerre avec l’Iran, la fermeture du détroit d’Ormuz, la situation au Liban et en Syrie, ainsi que le dossier israélo-palestinien. Point d'étape avec Johan Bodin, notre journaliste sur place.

france24fr.title: Mort de Philippe Bouvard : une voix de la radio s’éteint
france24fr.description: Le journaliste, animateur et écrivain Philippe Bouvard est mort ce lundi à l’âge de 96 ans, à son domicile de Cannes. Créateur et animateur historique des Grosses Têtes pendant 37 ans, Philippe Bouvard a marqué durablement la radio et la télévision françaises. Retiré des ondes depuis janvier 2025, il laisse derrière lui une carrière hors norme et plusieurs générations d’auditeurs. Reportage France 2.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation contre les mutilations génitales féminines à Paris
france24fr.description: Des centaines de personnes ont manifesté ce samedi à Paris pour dire non aux mutilations génitales féminines. Une mobilisation qui intervient après la diffusion d'une campagne pro-excision sur les réseaux sociaux au Mali.

france24fr.title: Iran : une économie exsangue sous la menace de nouvelles sanctions américaines
france24fr.description: L’économie iranienne s’enfonce dans la crise. L’inflation annuelle a atteint 66% en juillet, tandis que les prix à la consommation ont bondi de 87,9% sur un an ; pour l’alimentation, la hausse atteint 128%. Correspondance de Siavosh Ghazi depuis Téhéran.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : une primaire pour trouver un leader à gauche
france24fr.description: L’eurodéputé Raphaël Glucksmann a officialisé sa candidature et espère s’imposer comme le chef de file d’une gauche éclatée entre plusieurs prétendants. France 24 fait le point avec Jean Guarrigues, historien et politologue.

france24fr.title: En direct : Trump affirme que l'Iran "s'effondre", avant l'annonce de sanctions américaines
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a affirmé sur sa plateforme Truth Social que l'Iran "s'effondrait complètement", à quelques heures de l'annonce des détails de sanctions économiques américaines contre Téhéran La république islamique a par ailleurs balayé la menace américaine d'un "D-Day économique" visant à l'asphyxier, y voyant un "aveu de défaite" des États-Unis. Suivez notre direct.

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : plus de 2500 morts sur 5375 cas enregistrés en 100 jours
france24fr.description: 🇨🇩 100 jours après la déclaration de la 17ᵉ épidémie d’Ebola en RDC, la souche Bundibugyo reste sans vaccin. Les autorités cherchent à freiner la propagation du virus, un défi majeur dans un pays où les travailleurs venus de différentes régions se côtoient. L'épidémie a déjà fait plus de 2500 morts sur 5375 cas enregistrés.

zeit.title: Handyverbot an Schulen: Frankreichs Präsident setzt Handyverbot für Oberstufenschüler in Kraft
zeit.description: An Frankreichs Schulen gilt nun in allen Jahrgängen ein Handyverbot – von Grundschule bis Oberstufe. Das Verbot sei zum Schutz der Kinder, sagt Präsident Emmanuel Macron.

zeit.title: Unternehmen: Tschentscher würdigt Kühne: War ambitionierter Unternehmer
Dürre in Baden-Württemberg: Dürre bringt Höfe laut Bauernverband in Existenznöte
zeit.description: Trockenheit und Hitze haben der Ernte und der Futterversorgung im Südwesten Deutschlands stark zugesetzt. Der Bauernverband fordert schnelle Hilfen von Land und Bund.

zeit.title: US-Kanada-Handelskonflikt: Trump kündigt 50-Prozent-Zoll auf Autos, Lkw und Stahl aus Kanada an
zeit.description: Im Handelskonflikt mit Kanada setzt Donald Trump auf Eskalation. Der US-Präsident hat hohe Zölle auf Autos, große und kleine Lastwagen, Autoteile und Stahl angekündigt.

zeit.title: Deutsche Eishockey Liga: Nürnberg Ice Tigers mehrere Wochen ohne Neuzugang Dufour
Radsport: Dritte Etappe der Vuelta nach Unwetter abgebrochen
Frankreich: Der Mann, der Frankreich vor den Radikalen retten will
zeit.description: Der Linke Raphaël Glucksmann will französischer Präsident werden. Dafür müsste er nicht nur Marine Le Pen besiegen, sondern auch den noch linkeren Jean-Luc Mélenchon.

zeit.title: Chemie-Forschung: Chemieforschungszentrum eröffnet erste Büros in Merseburg
Unfall: 13-jähriges Mädchen von Lastwagen angefahren - Lebensgefahr
Klage gegen Erhöhungen: OLG Hamm sieht Verstöße bei Fernwärme-Preisklauseln von Eon
Kriminalität: Passant leiht Polizei sein E-Bike für Verfolgungsfahrt
Briefwahl: Wahlleitung Sachsen-Anhalt weist AfD-Behauptung zu Wahlbetrug zurück
zeit.description: Die Landeswahlleiterin in Sachsen-Anhalt verweist auf die Sicherheit der Briefwahl. Zuvor hatte Tino Chrupalla Zweifel an deren Rechtmäßigkeit geäußert.

zeit.title: Niederlande: Schock bei Oberstufenfahrt: Mehrere Verletzte nach Busunfall
Nachruf auf Klaus-Michael Kühne: Im Herzen Hamburger
zeit.description: Klaus-Michael Kühne wurde mit unternehmerischem Mut der zweitreichste Deutsche. Steuern zahlte er lieber in der Schweiz – trotzdem gab er seiner Heimat viel zurück.

zeit.title: UN-Mission: Zwei UN-Blauhelmsoldaten im Südsudan getötet
zeit.description: Im Südsudan sind nach Angaben der Vereinten Nationen zwei Blauhelmsoldaten getötet worden. Laut der UN-Mission fand der Angriff durch »bewaffnete Unbekannte« statt.

nzz.title: 35 Jahre ukrainische Unabhängigkeit: London gibt zum Jahrestag grünes Licht für den Transfer wichtiger Rüstungstechnologie
nzz.description: Präsident Selenski gibt sich am ukrainischen Unabhängigkeitstag kämpferisch und ruft die Partner zu mehr Unterstützung auf, vor allem bei der Flugabwehr. Die wichtigste Zusage des Tages betrifft aber Offensivwaffen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: «Koalition der Willigen» kontert Russlands Drohungen +++ EU unterstützt Ukraine mit 6,1 Milliarden Euro
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Dies sind die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: VIDEO - Das Öl sucht einen anderen Weg: die Alternativen zur Strasse von Hormuz
nzz.description: Durch die Strasse von Hormuz läuft rund ein Viertel des weltweiten Ölhandels auf dem Seeweg. Die Golfstaaten versuchen deshalb, ihre Abhängigkeit von der Meerenge zu verringern. Doch wie viel von Hormuz lässt sich tatsächlich ersetzen? Und welche neuen Risiken entstehen dabei?

nzz.title: Der rot-grüne Zürcher Stadtrat experimentierte auf der Bellerivestrasse mit einem Spurabbau. Jetzt beerdigt er die Idee
nzz.description: Auf der Einfallsachse vom rechten Seeufer her in die Stadt gilt bald wieder freie Fahrt.

nzz.title: Lösung für Cyberangriffe oder technische Störungen: In der Schweiz kann man bald auch offline mit Karte bezahlen
nzz.description: Regierung und Nationalbank haben mit der Privatwirtschaft eine Lösung erarbeitet, wie man auch ohne Datenverbindung mit Karten zahlen kann. Möglich ist dies aber nur für lebensnotwendige Produkte wie Lebensmittel oder Medikamente.

nzz.title: Breel Embolo bleibt unberechenbar: Viel Geld begleitet den Transfer des Schweizer Nationalspielers in die USA
nzz.description: Nach nur einem Jahr bricht der 29-jährige Stürmer das Langzeitprojekt bei Stade Rennes ab. Das zieht auch Irritationen nach sich. Doch der Wechsel von der Ligue 1 in die Major League Soccer zum Atlanta United FC hat ein Volumen von über 15 Millionen Euro.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - News aus Zürich: Der historische Hardturm war eigentlich eine «Hardburg»
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: Ausserordentliche Milliarden für die Armee – was würde das genau bedeuten?
nzz.description: Auch ausserordentliche Ausgaben müssen mittelfristig kompensiert werden. Wie schwierig das ist, zeigt sich bei den Corona-Schulden. Eine andere Variante wäre, den Kantonen ein paar Milliarden abzuzwacken.

nzz.title: Wer trägt die Schuld für die Toten von Bondo? Die angeklagte Nationalrätin Anna Giacometti sagt: «Man sperrt nicht einfach aus heiterem Himmel einen Wanderweg»
nzz.description: Ein Prozess am Regionalgericht Maloja soll klären, ob der Bergsturz von Bondo im Jahr 2017 vorhersehbar gewesen wäre. Die Bilanz des ersten Prozesstags.

nzz.title: High-Tech-Meisterschaften in Peking: Roboter läuft schneller als Usain Bolt, zerschellt aber im Ziel
nzz.description: An den World Humanoid Robot Games in China stellten Roboter mehrere Rekorde auf. Zwei Experten ordnen ein, was davon Show ist und was echter technologischer Fortschritt.

nzz.title: Bewerbungen ohne Fotos, Namen und Herkunftsangaben: Bringt Anonymität mehr Chancengerechtigkeit?
nzz.description: Am Montag diskutierte der Zürcher Kantonsrat über Diskriminierung im Bewerbungsverfahren. Die Mehrheit findet, die Kantonsverwaltung rekrutiere heute schon gut genug.

nzz.title: Die Zölle verderben Schweizer Maschinenherstellern das Geschäft im lukrativen amerikanischen Markt
nzz.description: Ein Exportvolumen von einer Milliarde Franken: So hoch waren die Einbussen für Schweizer Firmen aus dem MEM-Sektor 2025 wegen der amerikanischen Zölle. Noch immer ist das Geschäft rückläufig. Dafür erhofft man sich neue Chancen in China.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Handelsstreit: Trump lässt Handelskrieg mit Kanada weiter eskalieren
nzz.description: Im Februar hat der Supreme Court Trumps Zölle für unrechtmässig erklärt. Doch der amerikanische Präsident verursacht mit seinen umstrittenen Zöllen weiter weltweit Turbulenzen. Die neuesten Entwicklungen.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: USA wollen die «härtesten Sanktionen der Geschichte» gegen Iran vorstellen +++ Schiffsverkehr durch Hormuz stark eingeschränkt
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Frankreichs letzter Linksliberaler: Raphaël Glucksmann steigt in den Ring um die Präsidentschaft
nzz.description: Raphaël Glucksmann will 2027 französischer Präsident werden. Der Sozialdemokrat setzt auf eine gemässigte, proeuropäische Linke ohne Jean-Luc Mélenchon. Doch der radikale Volkstribun liegt in den Umfragen vor ihm.

nzz.title: Ein neuer Vorwurf gegen Jacques Moretti könnte eine Wende im Fall Crans-Montana bringen
nzz.description: Der Mitbetreiber der ausgebrannten Bar soll laut einem Medienbericht seine Frau spitalreif verletzt haben. Er sitzt deshalb erneut in Untersuchungshaft. Das wirft mehrere Fragen zum Strafverfahren auf.

observador.title: CGTP exige retirada do subsídio social de desemprego da PSU
observador.description: A central sindical alerta que a integração na Prestação Social Única reduz duração, valor e contribuições registadas para pensão dos desempregados sem acesso ao subsídio de desemprego.

observador.title: Talibãs proíbem por lei todas as manifestações
observador.description: Nova lei policial aprovada pelo líder supremo talibã elimina qualquer enquadramento jurídico para protestos e alarga poderes coercivos das forças de segurança.

observador.title: Papa assinala "momento difícil" do exército português
observador.description: O Papa evocou a parábola do Bom Samaritano para descrever os dois soldados mortos na autoestrada. Uma comitiva de 129 militares e forças de segurança esteve em audiência privada no Vaticano.

observador.title: CP adere ao passe intermodal de Coimbra em outubro
observador.description: A presidente da Câmara de Coimbra confirmou a adesão da CP ao bilhete Move-C na mesma data dos transportes intermunicipais. Em aberto fica o fim do transporte gratuito entre as estações.

observador.title: Sindicato acusa Governo de "propaganda" nos registos
observador.description: O STRN questiona os 26 mil processos anunciados pelo Ministério da Justiça: entre maio e junho, os serviços com atraso aumentaram 82% e os dias de atraso mais do que duplicaram.

observador.title: 17h. André Ventura reitera que MAI não tem "condições " p...
observador.description: O líder do Chega acusa Luís Montenegro de estar "comprometido" com a situação. Ainda, o PS acusa o Governo de tentar "criar medo" à volta da sustentabilidade da Segurança Social.

observador.title: Bruno Alves integra equipa técnica de Jesus na Seleção
observador.description: Antigo defesa internacional regressa a uma casa que conhece bem. Foram 96 jogos pela Seleção, com 11 golos e cinco assistências ao longo de uma década a representar as cores de Portugal.

observador.title: Escolas primárias vão prever desemprego dos alunos?
observador.description: O Reino Unido quer identificar alunos em risco de desemprego logo aos 4 anos. Eduardo Sá analisa os perigos de avaliar a infância sob a pressão da produtividade e das métricas do mercado de trabalho.

observador.title: Metro de Lisboa prolonga horário durante festival Kalorama
observador.description: Linhas vermelha e verde com serviço alargado nas noites de sexta a domingo. Estação Bela Vista, a mais próxima do festival, é a recomendada pelo Metro.

observador.title: Caiu chuva, granizo e a etapa: Vuelta anula última subida
observador.description: Intempérie no final da primeira das últimas duas subidas anulou terceira etapa, quando Wenzel e Fortunato tinham 20 segundos de avanço sobre o pelotão, mas houve outro nome a assumir "protagonismo".

observador.title: "Mais vagas em Medicina não resolve o SNS"
observador.description: A ANEM defende que redistribuir vagas existentes pelo interior é preferível a criar novos cursos. Hospitais do litoral já estão no limite para receber estagiários.

observador.title: "Ucrânia está longe de ceder à Rússia"
observador.description: Coronel José do Carmo diz que a Ucrânia está mais forte apesar dos problemas com falta de armamento. Sublinha ainda que resiliência ucraniana se mantém e que a ausência de fundos não é problemática.

observador.title: Calor extremo de 2026 na Europa será o "novo normal"
observador.description: Portugal registou 680 óbitos acima do esperado. A Sardenha chegou aos 48,4 graus. Para os climatologistas, este verão extremo é apenas um ensaio do que aí vem.

observador.title: Alenquer acusa Governo de "injustiça" nos apoios
observador.description: O autarca afirma que "houve uma injustiça e falta de equidade" para com a cidade e pede reavaliação da quantia, visto ter recebido uma quantia substancialmente inferior a outros municípios.

observador.title: Operações stop: GNR detém 16 pessoas em Abufeira e Loulé
observador.description: Foram apreendidas grandes quantidades de droga durante operações de fiscalização rodoviárias da GNR. Dez das detenções foram feitas por condução com excesso de álcool no sangue.

observador.title: "Um manguito à zona euro": Paris critica plano de Mélenchon
observador.description: O ministro Lescure alerta que recomprar 20% da dívida pelo Banco de França faria disparar os custos de financiamento do país e equivalia a sair do euro de facto.

observador.title: Chega questiona futuro da estrada Furnas-Povoação
observador.description: Partido critica falta de informação sobre projeto, financiamento e calendário da obra. A primeira fase, inaugurada em abril de 2025, custou 7,7 milhões de euros.

observador.title: 16h. Zelensky diz que nada pode pôr em causa independência
observador.description: Presidente do Conselho Europeu, António Costa, também discursou na cerimónia dos 35 anos de independência da Ucrânia. Ainda, Ordem dos Médicos está preocupada com a situação do INEM.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: Milliardär Klaus-Michael Kühne ist tot, Raphaël Glucksmann will französischer Präsident werden,Trinkgeld per Karte
spiegel.description: Der Milliardär Klaus-Michael Kühne ist tot. Raphaël Glucksmann will Frankreichs Präsident werden, deshalb gibt seine Partnerin die Moderation der TV-Nachrichten ab. Und Verbraucherschützer kritisieren die Trinkgeldfunktion. Das ist die Lage am Montagabend.

spiegel.title: Tortenwerfer Noël Godin: Er rief »Gloup! Gloup!« – dann flog die Torte in das Gesicht von Bill Gates
spiegel.description: Der Künstler Noël Godin protestierte auf besondere Art: Er zielte mit Sahnetorten auf Prominente. Ein Opfer traf es ganze achtmal, auch Bill Gates musste Sahne schlucken. Nun ist Godin gestorben.

spiegel.title: »Washington Post«: Karen Attiah wurde wegen Posts zu Charlie Kirks Tod gefeuert – nun soll sie in den Job zurück
spiegel.description: Ist es ein Kündigungsgrund, wenn eine Kolumnistin meinungsstark schreibt? So sah es die »Washington Post«, als Karen Attiah um Charlie Kirk »nicht theatralisch trauern« wollte. Eine Schlichterin nannte die Entlassung unbegründet.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump kündigt weitere Zölle von 50 Prozent gegen Kanada an
spiegel.description: US-Präsident Trump lässt den Handelskonflikt mit Kanada eskalieren: Ab Januar sollen Importabgaben für Autos, Lastwagen, Autoteile und Stahl steigen. Mit wütenden Beschuldigungen reagiert er auf eine Ansage von Premier Carney.

spiegel.title: Sebastian Vettel: Ex-Formel-1-Weltmeister will nun das Segeln lernen
spiegel.description: Viermal gewann Sebastian Vettel den Titel als Formel-1-Weltmeister, nach dem Ende seiner Laufbahn wurde er Miteigentümer eines Segelteams. Nun will er den Sport selbst lernen. Der 39-Jährige hat Respekt vor der Aufgabe.

spiegel.title: US-Midterms: Dan Sullivan unterstützt Dan Sullivan – aber NICHT Dan Sullivan
spiegel.description: Einem war das bizarre Zerren im Midterms-Wahlkampf in Alaska noch nicht verwirrend genug: Dan Sullivan. Er hat sich in den Streit von Dan Sullivan und Dan Sullivan eingeschaltet. Ja, Sie lesen richtig.

spiegel.title: Italien: Regierung plant Bußgelder für abgelenkte Fußgänger mit Handy
spiegel.description: Smartphone-Zombies auf Italiens Straßen sollen künftig zahlen: Ein Entwurf der neuen Straßenverkehrsordnung sieht Bußgelder für abgelenkte Fußgänger vor.

spiegel.title: Günzburg: 30 Fledermäuse nisten sich während Urlaub in Wohnung ein
spiegel.description: Nach ihrem Urlaub hatte eine Frau aus Bayern etwa 30 neue Mitbewohner: Fledermäuse waren durch ein Kippfenster in ihre Wohnung gelangt. So schützen Sie sich vor den nachtaktiven Tieren zu Hause.

spiegel.title: Kartoffeln in Deutschland: Was Extremwetter und Dürre für den Anbau bedeuten
spiegel.description: Trockenheit, Starkregen, Schädlinge: Extremjahre werden immer mehr zum Normalfall. Was das für Nutzpflanzen bedeutet, erklärt der Bodenökologe Martin Schädler. Er simuliert Zukunftsklima auf echten Äckern.

spiegel.title: Immobilien: Warum es gut wäre, wenn die Mieten stärker steigen dürften
spiegel.description: Enteignen oder Baugesellschaft gründen: Um hohe Mieten zu bekämpfen, rufen Politiker und Aktivisten nach mehr Staat. Helfen könnte ein radikal neuer Ansatz.

spiegel.title: Pazifik: Zwei Tote bei erneutem US-Angriff gegen mutmaßliches Drogenschmuggelboot
spiegel.description: Die USA haben abermals ein Boot im Pazifik angegriffen, dabei wurden zwei mutmaßliche Drogenschmuggler getötet. Die Militäreinsätze sind hochumstritten.

spiegel.title: Pfaffenhofen an der Ilm: Wie ein halbes Brot eine Bäckerei aus Bayern 15.000 Euro kostete

phys-org.title: Soil bacteria share amino acids, helping nearly half survive nutrient gaps
phys-org.description: Bacteria, too, depend on good neighborly relations: A new study by the Osnabrück University, in collaboration with researchers from the University of Cambridge in England, shows that soil bacteria live in beneficial communities and frequently exchange nutrients with one another. The study, led by Prof. Dr. Christian Kost, has now been published in the journal Nature Microbiology.

phys-org.title: Floating wetlands slash wastewater greenhouse gas emissions, according to study
phys-org.description: A world-first trial of floating wetland pods in wastewater lagoons shows they cut greenhouse gas emissions by more than a quarter, highlighting their potential as a nature-based solution for decarbonizing the water sector.

phys-org.title: Tiny root hairs, big impact: How bacteria help plants survive drought
phys-org.description: What helps plants cope better with drought? With heat waves and periods of extreme drought becoming increasingly common worldwide, the need for drought-tolerant plants is increasingly urgent. With the help of bacteria, plants can unlock traits that help them cope with drought, securing biodiversity and food safety.

phys-org.title: As California embraces universal transitional kindergarten, the state's other child-care workers are struggling
phys-org.description: Last spring, UC Berkeley researcher Anna Powell sat in on a Zoom call as a number of Bay Area child care center leaders discussed, with sympathy and frustration, the difficult position their businesses were in.

phys-org.title: Antarctic bacteria share 'life‑support' genes to survive extreme conditions
phys-org.description: Antarctica is one of the driest, coldest places on Earth. Very little life survives its extremes. In the soils scattered around the frozen ice sheets, however, communities of microbes do survive. And one of the keys to their success is a surprisingly communal strategy.

phys-org.title: A forecast is not a decision: Design engineering for drought preparedness
phys-org.description: More than 80 countries face chronic drought, yet only a third have systems in place to act before a drought arrives rather than after. The gap is costly. According to the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, every $1 invested in anticipatory action can save up to $7 in averted losses, while also helping protect lives and livelihoods before crisis conditions take hold. Acting early works. So why don't more countries do it?

phys-org.title: Climate scientists solve monsoon puzzle and warn of risks to fisheries
phys-org.description: A new study has reconciled a long-standing paradox in the South Asian summer monsoon cycle. Climate scientists have discovered why geological records from land and sea have told opposite stories about monsoons throughout history and found that rising temperatures over Southern Africa reduce upwelling in the Arabian Sea, which could damage marine productivity and fisheries. The work is published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

phys-org.title: Making the case for independent science
phys-org.description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule ended in the spring, when voters replaced him with Péter Magyar, who has pledged to undo Orbán-led initiatives that, in the eyes of critics, isolated and politicized science.

phys-org.title: Hidden in plain sight: New evidence links Henry VIII's lost castle to Dover Castle
phys-org.description: Dr. Christopher Moore, a research fellow and former Ph.D. researcher in hidden and lost heritage at Kent, combined archive records with architectural evidence to link the 1883–84 extension to Sandown Castle, one of Henry VIII's 16th-century coastal forts. Supported by the university and carried out with the cooperation of English Heritage, the research offers fresh insight into the history of Dover Castle and the story of one of England's lost Tudor fortresses.

phys-org.title: Tiny ocean plankton hold clues to the future of Maine lobster
phys-org.description: The future of Maine's lobster industry may depend on a creature the size of a sesame seed. Researchers at the University of Maine have discovered that planktonic baby lobsters, or larvae, preferentially feed on Calanus finmarchicus, a tiny, calorie-rich zooplankton species, during one of the most vulnerable stages of their lives. Their new study upholds a theory advanced by scientists in the past decade that may be relevant to recent declines in Maine's lobster harvest.

phys-org.title: Borneo forest fires spike again: Why El Niño isn't the sole culprit
phys-org.description: Forest and land fires across Indonesia have spiked once again. News and social media in the country are flooded with images of thick plumes of smoke from Kalimantan (or Borneo)—the world's third-largest island—that are choking residential areas and even drifting into neighboring countries.

phys-org.title: LST-1 and MAGIC telescopes shatter distance record for the very high-energy blazar OP 313
phys-org.description: On Aug. 15, the CTAO LST Collaboration and the MAGIC Collaboration released findings from observations of OP 313, the most distant very-high-energy blazar ever recorded. The paper, published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, presents in-depth observations conducted with the prototype Large-Sized Telescope (LST-1) and the MAGIC telescopes at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory in La Palma, Spain.

phys-org.title: Reframing Homer's Sirens through gender, nature and social order
phys-org.description: Though they are pivotal to Homer's epic, luring Odysseus with the promise of eternal wisdom, the Greek poet barely described the mysterious Sirens. What might a better understanding of these formless, disembodied feminine creatures contribute to this timeless teaching myth?

phys-org.title: How chromosomes find their partners
phys-org.description: For a long time, so-called satellite DNA was considered largely worthless. Now, ETH Zurich researchers have shown in fruit flies that these repetitive sections of genetic material act as a kind of barcode, enabling the correct chromosomes to recognize one another.

phys-org.title: Scientists identify design rules for the best thermoelectric materials
phys-org.description: Researchers from Tokyo Metropolitan University have used a theoretical framework to derive design rules for creating new thermoelectric materials. The efficiency of converting thermal energy to electricity is often determined by parameters that strongly depend on each other, making it difficult to identify ideal recipes.

phys-org.title: GenAI cannot accurately grade student essays in higher education, study finds
phys-org.description: New research from Cardiff University and the University of Melbourne has investigated whether GenAI could mimic human marking when evaluating written student work. The results have been published in the journal Assessment & Evaluation in Higher Education.

phys-org.title: New free-space optical link adds a wireless component to the nation's longest quantum network
phys-org.description: There's a new lighthouse on Long Island. But instead of shining light to guide ships through waterways, this one transmits and receives particles of light that carry quantum information. Perched atop a seven-story building at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Brookhaven National Laboratory, the "Quantum Lighthouse" is a key pillar of the free-space optical (FSO) link spanning Brookhaven Lab, the State University of New York at Stony Brook (Stony Brook University) and Yale Universit

phys-org.title: Long-term study reveals hidden threat of schistosomiasis in endangered chimpanzees
phys-org.description: A 12-year study of rescued chimpanzees at the Ngamba Island Chimpanzee Sanctuary (NICS) in Uganda has revealed persistent intestinal schistosomiasis infections, highlighting the need for long-term disease surveillance to protect endangered wildlife.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

proj-syn.title: The Age of Gated Recessions
proj-syn.description: Aggregate economic indicators are obscuring a widening divide between those enjoying rapid income growth and those facing deteriorating job prospects. The rise of AI could deepen this disparity, with certain regions and workers experiencing recession-like conditions while others enjoy boom times.

proj-syn.title: The AI Curse
proj-syn.description: Every sanction that ordinary citizens have ever possessed—the ability to withhold labor, taxes, sons, or votes—presupposes someone who needs what you can withhold. As AI infrastructure encroaches on Americans, they are learning the lesson of many resource-rich states: where there is no need, there is no democracy.

proj-syn.title: Where Will the Global Bond Rout Hit Growth and Equities?
proj-syn.description: In the US, the recent rise in bond yields is largely driven by structural factors like the end of the post-2008 Great Stagnation, higher potential growth from tech-industry investments, and greater private-sector demand for credit. Higher yields are more worrisome for advanced economies that are stagnating and innovating less.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Korean Catastrophe
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump seems not to appreciate that deterrence depends on the ability to mount a credible defense. This makes the Korean Peninsula a more dangerous place, not least because 28,000 US troops are stationed in South Korea, which the US is obliged by treaty to defend.

proj-syn.title: The Dollar’s Outer Defenses Have Been Breached
proj-syn.description: The puzzle of why the Trump administration is so concerned with a falling yen has historical parallels not to the 1930s or the 1980s, but to the 1960s, when US officials feared that a crisis elsewhere could spread to America. With US bond yields spiking, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is getting desperate.

proj-syn.title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
proj-syn.description: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity, despite the many reasons that investors have to pursue greater diversification.

proj-syn.title: Aging Populations Need Not Mean Frailer Economies
proj-syn.description: Governments and economists have long viewed demographic aging as a threat to economic growth. But new research finds that labor scarcity encourages investment and shifts innovation toward labor-saving technologies, boosting productivity enough to offset a shrinking workforce.

proj-syn.title: Who’s Afraid of Chinese Surpluses?
proj-syn.description: China recorded the largest trade surplus in history last year, and its exports continue to grow. But the scale of the threat to the global economy, and the appropriate response, remains subject to considerable disagreement. Some economists advocate protectionist measures, if only to pressure China to commit to economic rebalancing, others argue that tariffs won’t help, and still other

proj-syn.title: Only Protectionism Can Safeguard European Industry
proj-syn.description: While economic rebalancing by China would be good for everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in this direction. With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.

proj-syn.title: The Gospel of the Great Leader
proj-syn.description: North Korea’s communist regime has long functioned as a faith, repurposing Christian doctrine and imagery to deify its founder, Kim Il-sung, and his descendants. A new book traces how those religious influences transformed the Kim dynasty’s personality cult into a system that has endured across three generations.

proj-syn.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
proj-syn.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

proj-syn.title: Superintelligent Democracy
proj-syn.description: Rather than framing the pursuit of AI capabilities as a race, we should turn the process into a democratic mission, with milestones set by the people, rather than on their behalf. Taiwan's own demonstration of mission-led governance, along with insights from the open-web community, show what is possible.

proj-syn.title: How Europe Can Save a Trillion Euros and Win the AI Race
proj-syn.description: If the risk Europe faces is losing access to frontier AI models, the solution is not necessarily to chase the labs that created them in the hopes of eventually pulling ahead.
